prs.title: Run Desktop on Windows with a WSL2 bridge, and check it from WSL2
prs.note: The original branch, kept as the reference and index. On 22 Oct a merge of main (749b2c1) took the rebased series' tree, so it stays byte-identical to the stack plus the spikes draft. Review happens in the stacked PRs.

prs.title: Fixes for every platform: browser extension, approvals across a seal, SecretSpec deadline
prs.note: Reviewable and testable on Linux. Browser extension and prompt fixes, pending approvals kept across a seal, SecretSpec answered before its 30 s deadline, claim env vars, category-list layout.

prs.title: Windows fixes: unseal without admin, parser spawn, pipe buffer, console window, tray
prs.note: No WSL. hardwareseal 0.1.2, the parser spawn and 512-byte pipe buffer fixes split out of the broker's first live run, connection-failure events, icon, no console window, tray click, and build-windows.sh.

prs.title: Add an experimental WSL2 interop broker for the vault's named pipe
prs.note: Protocol v19 (WSL origin hint): main took 17 (Desktop revamp) and 18 (launch chain). Grants for relayed requests capped at five minutes. Approved through the CLI or #44's popup.

prs.title: Show the permission approval popup on every platform, with checks driven from WSL2
prs.note: Largest PR. Popup port (now on main's permission watcher), input guard, taskbar flash, stays open on seal, plus the check harness. Also: a request asked again changes the permission revision, so main's popup shows it again (found by the seal check).

prs.title: Check one-time SecretSpec writes from WSL2
prs.note: Its SecretSpec changes are in main since 21 Oct (cherry-picked 5523e8a..d078679, adapted in 749b2c1, protocol v18). What remains is check.sh write-once, which needs #44's harness.

prs.title: Expose the approval popup and main window to screen readers and UI Automation
prs.note: Split out of the popup PR because the popup's accessible text names the SecretSpec prompts.

prs.title: Bring the browser prompt forward on Windows, and check the extension in Edge and Chrome from WSL2
prs.note: browser-check.sh covers acceptance items 2-8, 12 and 13; adapted on 22 Oct to main's extension UX (field button, save question).

prs.title: Notes and a Claude Code skill for the Windows Desktop checks
prs.note: Optional, draft. AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md and a devenv-generated skill that documents the check scripts, so it sits on top of the stack. Nothing depends on it.

prs.title: Record the WSL2 transport spikes
prs.note: Optional, draft, independent of everything else. Three standalone crates outside the workspace: Hyper-V sockets, mirrored loopback with a token, interop.
